timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Our SOC has alerts. Does that mean we have coverage?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Not necessarily. You may have twenty alerts for phishing and nothing for lateral movement.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: ATT&CK organizes attacker behavior into tactics and techniques, like persistence, discovery, and exfiltration.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So we map detections to techniques?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Then you see which behaviors are detected, blocked, logged, or completely invisible.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What if a technique has no detection?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: That becomes a design requirement: new telemetry, analytics, control changes, or accepted risk.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Very much. It turns security monitoring from vibes into a coverage model.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So fewer random alerts, more intentional detection?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. We are hunting attackers, not collecting beeps.
